memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: episodic vertigo triggered by head movements.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: She reports brief spells of spinning sensation lasting seconds to minutes when looking up or rolling over in bed, associated with nausea but no hearing loss or tinnitus. Episodes occur 2-3 times per week.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg, weight 62 kg, height 158 cm, BMI 24.8 (overweight). General appearance alert. Otoscopic examination normal. Dix-Hallpike test positive for right posterior canal BPPV (torsional nystagmus). Neurologic exam otherwise normal.
IMPRESSION: Benign positional vertigo, right posterior canal. Advised on vestibular rehabilitation exercises. BMI overweight – counselled on balanced diet and regular activity. No hypertension or hyperglycemia noted.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start betahistine 16 mg twice daily. Review response in 6 weeks. Return if vertigo worsens, new headache, double vision, difficulty walking, hearing loss, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Betahistine 16 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily after meals. Continue for 8 weeks, then review.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Vestibular assessment: Dix-Hallpike test positive for right posterior canal BPPV (torsional up‑beating nystagmus). Audiometry (pure tone) shows hearing thresholds within normal limits bilaterally (0‑25 dB HL).

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.2 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.4 mmol/L (<2.6), HDL 1.3 mmol/L (>1.0), triglycerides 1.1 mmol/L (<1.7).
Fasting blood glucose: 5.4 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: follow‑up on vertigo and medication tolerance.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Vertigo frequency reduced to about once per week, milder, still triggered by sudden head movement. No nausea. Reports occasional mild dizziness when standing quickly.
EXAMINATION: BP 130/80 mmHg, weight 63 kg, BMI 25.1 (obese). ENT exam normal. Dix‑Hallpike now negative.
IMPRESSION: Improving BPPV on betahistine. BMI obese – reinforce diet and activity advice. Continue betahistine; add meclizine for acute episodes.
ARRANGEMENTS: Add meclizine 25 mg as needed for vertigo, max three times daily. Review in 8 weeks. Return if vertigo becomes daily, hearing loss, neurological signs, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Meclizine 25 mg tablet – take one tablet at onset of vertigo, not exceeding three doses in 24 hours. Use only as needed.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Repeat fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 4.0 mmol/L, LDL 2.2 mmol/L, HDL 1.4 mmol/L, triglycerides 1.0 mmol/L.
Fasting blood glucose: 5.2 mmol/L.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: increase in vertigo episodes and weight concern.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Vertigo now occurring 3‑4 times per week, lasting up to a minute, sometimes with mild nausea. Reports feeling heavier and less active.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/82 mmHg, weight 66 kg, BMI 26.4 (obese). ENT normal. No abnormal eye movements.
IMPRESSION: Possible breakthrough BPPV; consider vestibular rehab reinforcement. BMI obese – stress diet, aerobic activity 150 min/week, and weight monitoring.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue betahistine 16 mg BD. Continue meclizine SOS. Refer for supervised vestibular physiotherapy. Return if vertigo becomes constant, hearing loss, new headache, limb weakness, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Repeat audiometry: hearing thresholds stable, 0‑20 dB HL across frequencies, no new loss.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: post‑rehab assessment and medication review.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Vertigo episodes down to twice per week, milder, usually resolved with meclizine. No nausea. Feels more energetic after starting walks.
EXAMINATION: BP 129/78 mmHg, weight 65 kg, BMI 26.0 (obese). ENT normal. Dix‑Hallpike negative.
IMPRESSION: Vertigo improving with rehab and medication. Continue current regimen; reinforce lifestyle measures.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue betahistine 16 mg BD and meclizine 25 mg SOS. Encourage daily 30‑min brisk walk and reduced refined carbs. Return if vertigo increases, hearing changes, chest pain, breathlessness, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment changed: original follow‑up scheduled for 2026-07-12 moved to 2026-07-05 at 10:30 am per patient request due to travel plans.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine review and annual labs.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Vertigo episodes now once per week, mild, quickly relieved by meclizine. No falls. Reports stable weight.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/76 mmHg, weight 64 kg, BMI 25.6 (obese). ENT normal.
IMPRESSION: Stable BPPV on betahistine and meclizine SOS. BMI obese – reiterate diet and activity advice. Annual lipids and glucose within target.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue betahistine 16 mg BD. Continue meclizine 25 mg SOS as needed. Return if vertigo worsens, hearing loss, neurological symptoms, chest pain, breathlessness, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Annual fasting lipid profile: Total cholesterol 3.9 mmol/L (<5.2), LDL 2.1 mmol/L (<2.6), HDL 1.5 mmol/L (>1.0), triglycerides 0.9 mmol/L (<1.7).
Fasting blood glucose: 5.0 mmol/L (3.9‑5.5).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: final check‑up before year end.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Vertigo occasional, less than once per week, mild, self‑limited. No adverse effects from meds.
EXAMINATION: BP 127/75 mmHg, weight 63.5 kg, BMI 25.4 (obese). ENT normal.
IMPRESSION: Well‑controlled benign positional vertigo. Continue betahistine and meclizine SOS. Lifestyle advice maintained.
ARRANGEMENTS: No change in medication. Return if vertigo becomes frequent, hearing loss, new neurologic signs, chest pain, breathlessness, or fever >39°C.
